content:
This is a key observation in https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/08/18/palomar-a-registry-of-lean-verified-mathematics/ — “check… that the formal statements also match (in a semantic sense) the informal description of the claimed results”

How does Palomar plan to tackle this? The ML practitioner in me might suggest an initial benchmark dataset based on “translation” between informal and formal statements to measure accuracy of this task (for a given language model and prompt), however, this statistical approach doesn’t seem bulletproof in they way we may require.

Maybe we can use multiple models and measure the inter annotator agreement, e.g., so that we only admit a faithful translation if there is total agreement. This would not eliminate false positives but could help with robustness.

Open to thoughts here!

@Alex Korbonits, so far we just trust Sol to get it right. :woman_shrugging:

I would love to have someone do some research here, and propose alternative practical mechanisms (at no greater cost).

The palomar database gives anyone interested in doing this a great initial problem set to look at!
